searchText: This has implications for my [Grandine EPF project](https://github.com/eth-protocol-fellows/cohort-seven/pull/297), which currently includes recursive proof verification and replacing proof RPC sync. With recursion moving out of EIP-8025, what's the intended sync model? Can proof synchronization still work with gossip alone, or does proof-by-range/root RPC need to come back into scope? I wouldn't constraint the EPF project by any decision we make reg recursion in 8025. That decision is accounting for resources capacity in mainnet, and ACD decisions. I believe if recursion was a target explores in that project, that's still a fantastic target and IMHO should not be canceled. We will need recursion sooner or later. If that's within 8025 scope or not is more relates to other practicalities. From am EPF project perspective, I would say is more valuable to not feel tightly couples with scoping of real mainnet. Reg syncing I would say the project can decide whatever feels more interesting or fits time constrains for it. That makes sense. The challenge is that our project is focused on verification. Is there an existing recursive prover we could work against? Zisk has this capability, although haven't checked in their latest release if still works fine. But prob should.
